{{short description|Mathematician}}
'''Charlotte Bolette Sophie, Baroness Wedell-Wedellsborg'''  (27 January 1862 – 22 July 1953){{r|sss}} was one of four women mathematicians to attend the inaugural [[International Congress of Mathematicians]], held in Zurich in 1897.{{r|curbera|eminger}}

==Early life and background==
Wedell was originally from [[Denmark]],{{r|cat}} the daughter of {{ill|Vilhelm Ferdinand, Baron Wedell-Wedellsborg|da|Vilhelm Wedell-Wedellsborg (1827–1914)}} (of the [[Wedel (family)|Wedel noble family]]) and Louise Marie Sophie, Countess Schulin, and the granddaughter of {{ill|Johan Sigismund Schulin (1808–1880)|da}}.{{r|sss}}

==Career==
At the time of the Congress, in 1897, she had just completed a doctorate at the [[University of Lausanne]] in [[Switzerland]], with [[Adolf Hurwitz]] as an unofficial mentor.{{r|fenster}} The subject of her dissertation was the application of [[elliptic function]]s to the construction of the [[Malfatti circles]].{{r|cat|diss}}

At the congress, Wedell was listed as being affiliated with the [[University of Göttingen]]. The other three women at the congress were Iginia Massarini, Vera von Schiff, and [[Charlotte Scott]]. None were speakers; the first Congress with a woman as a speaker was in 1912.{{r|eminger}}

==Personal life==
Wedell married engineer Eugène Tomasini in Copenhagen in 1898; they divorced in 1909.{{r|sss}}
